# Hardware Description Languages with Verilog

::: {.lab-hero-lead}
Prepare for the HDL laboratory assignments. You will model combinational and sequential circuits in Verilog, check them with a test bench, and learn which coding styles a synthesis tool can turn into hardware.
:::

## How to read this handbook

| Element | What it tells you |
|:--|:--|
| Key Concept | A definition or idea you need before moving on. |
| Remember | A rule of thumb to keep in mind while coding. |
| Important Note | A rule or restriction that causes errors if ignored. |
| Technical Detail | Extra precision for readers who want the full picture. |
| Example | A numbered HDL example, shown with a copyable code block. |

Code blocks have a copy button in the top-right corner. Figures keep their original numbers (for example, Figure 3.37), so you can match them to your lecture notes. Use the search box in the top bar to find any keyword.
